Reading this as: the fast track runs on the 0.9 floor alone, no passing calibration required (your option 2). I'll record that as a decision superseding DEC-018 and make the change in a worktree.

Done. The fast track now runs on the 0.9 floor alone, landed in main as merge 0621dab1 (branch commit 399fc6e7), and `plumb jev status` in your repo now says `auto-approve: on`, in effect.

**What changed, per your decision (recorded as DEC-143, superseding DEC-120):**
- JEV's verdict clears a record when every part scores strictly above the floor. A passing calibration of the same JEV version and question form raises the floor to its threshold. A missing, failed, other-version or other-form calibration is simply ignored. Nothing is suspended any more.
- The owner's switch checks only that JEV is configured and reachable with its credential.
- The approval re-check demands a calibration only when an approval cites one, so earlier calibrated approvals still re-check as before.
- The records follow: SR-250 (statement, EX-5, EX-6), SR-242 EX-10, SR-244 EX-3, SR-252 (title, EX-1, EX-6) and INT-083's will. README and docs/concept.md stop saying the switch is refused without a calibration.

**Verification.** The capture and understand test directories ran green after four tests were rewritten to the new rule, plus the bundle and auto-approve tests in main after the merge. The 62 links the merge would have left stale are repinned. Validate shows only the two pre-existing DEC-072 errors.

**What happens next, without you:** the judge job will now fast-track any proposed record JEV scores above 0.9 from your logged words, and send the rest through question rounds. The 170 records waiting on a judge get processed as sessions run the job.

Skipped: the worktree at C:\coding\plumb-wt\floor is left in place because removing it would delete five judgment log files the deny rule stops me copying into main; `/plumb jev calibrate` stays optional and yours.
